design_rationale:
WORKLOG / DOSSIER — task 0 (flood_coverage_and_mortgagee_billing).
[Draw] draw_counts.py --task 0: prerequisite_problems=2, factor_counts=[4, 6, 5]; the offer took 6 factors, the renewal 5, the payment 4.
[Why a good test] Rosalind asks only to pay her flood renewal. The KB never states a payment amount on its own: the payment rule waits on the new-term premium charge (state form), the renewal rule waits on the indicated premium (state form), and the records show neither exists (indicated_renewal_premium empty, last charge for term 2025-09-03). The agent must find the offer and the renewal problems, rate the missed offer (6 rules), fix the renewal term premium (5 rules, including where the loyalty clock starts) and then price the payment (4 rules) on the world each write leaves. Difficulty comes from policy reading, ledger reconciliation (15 billing rows, 5 claim rows) and cross-product reads (HomeGuard, LandlordGuard lookup, umbrella and its underlying ledger), not from tool choice: each problem has exactly one write tool named by its policy.
[Scope] Already occupied: nothing (first task). This task claims flood_ext_renewal_indication, flood_ext_renewal_term, flood_ext_renewal_payment and tools record_flood_renewal_offer_81f1ff73, renew_flood_policy_8cc307a9, pay_flood_renewal_premium_ad8d78a5 (owner=user). Left for task 1: the midterm limit-increase billing, the insured's signed cancellation with its credit, and the refund — a disjoint write space (flood_additional_premium, flood_policy_cancelled/flood_return_premium, flood_refund_issued) with its own draw (2 prerequisite problems, factors 4/6/5).
[Problem-tree card] root flood_ext_renewal_payment (user tool pay_flood_renewal_premium_ad8d78a5). Edge 1: payment -> flood_ext_renewal_term, value_input, gate new_term_premium, form state, sentence 'A renewal payment is not taken until the premium account carries the premium charge for the new term.' (negated direction; only the renewal write posts a new-term premium charge). False at the opening: flood_billing 2d7adc7c-16b0-43d6-be1e-3ddaae4ac973 is the latest charge, term 2025-09-03. Edge 2: renewal -> flood_ext_renewal_indication, state_gate (revised in round 2 from value_input), gate flood_policies.indicated_renewal_premium, form state, sentence 'The renewal term premium is fixed only after the indicated premium for the upcoming term stands on the policy.' (affirmative; only the offer writes indicated_renewal_premium). False at the opening: indicated_renewal_premium ''. On this world the capped premium 282.60 is the smaller figure, so the edge bears weight as a gate, not as a value (any indicated premium >= 282.60 gives the same term premium); the value_input floor max(2-1,1)=1 is met by edge 1. Four-point test on both: ordering connective (not until / only after), record-visible state, no tool/id/code token, strength matches condition. Topological order offer -> renewal -> payment; no parallel edge. Deletion sensitivity (run): skip renewal -> payment formula 448.56 instead of 304.24; skip offer -> renewal recompute raises on the empty indicated premium. No tool validates a prerequisite; the persona hints nothing.
[Base-invariant card] offer (flood_renewal_offered): flood_premium_rating and flood_renewal, no gate on the offer -> policy_scope. renewal (flood_policy_renewed): flood_agg_companion_discount, flood_premium_rating (policy_scope) and flood_renewal.renewal_grace: anchor flood_policies.expiration_date 2026-09-03, 30 calendar days (variants.renewal_grace_days), not_after, inclusive -> last on-time day 2026-10-03; frozen 2026-09-24 inside; 2026-10-04 would fail. payment (flood_payment_received): flood_billing_and_mortgagee, billable_status applies only to premium billing -> policy_scope.
[Business-object card] Object: flood policy FG-5207-4418 (b77deded-a4c6-4898-9b0d-d89d143716b3); correlation key flood_policy_id. The payment's earlier balance aggregates every billing row of this policy (charges 1882.56 incl. the new term's 262.82 premium and 50.00 fee, credits 1582.24); the 2022 returned payment c9fc8d6f-2f7d-47ab-984f-517c76160dd8 references bae563fc-9d83-48eb-a637-2523b2d7f5ae and its fee 6fb9d5fd-7ed9-4d3f-bdb9-157ee79811fc references the return; the 2022-09-06 payment settled them. Nothing on the HomeGuard/umbrella is written.
[Factor card] offer: rated_building_amount_rule (M) replacement cost 238000 < limit 250000 -> 238000 (baseline -> 471.83); newly_mapped_building_rate (P) AE + revision 13 months -> 1.45 (-> 830.86); flood_loss_load (P) one 2021 payment, none in 36 months -> 5% (-> 436.31; near-miss: the 2024 claim is a denial); elevation_credit_after_claims (P) -> 5% (-> 472.64); construction_era_adjustment (P, cross home) built 1962 -> +10% (-> 420.63); companion_discount_tenure (P, cross home, multi-source) 208 months -> 8% (-> 493.01). Whole baseline 868.80. renewal: renewal_cap_tenure (P, multi-source) counted tenure 65 months, no claim payment in 60 -> 15 - 3 = 12% (baseline tier cap 15% -> 269.86); cap_tenure_start (M, anchor family, cross home) a claim payment within 120 months restarts the clock at 2021-04-14 -> 65 months (baseline: from the 2016-09-03 original effective date, 120 months, loyal 8% -> 253.43; near-miss: the HomeGuard began in 2009, but the household-start tier needs a claim-free lookback); prompt_payment_credit (P, multi-source) 2% (near-miss: the 2022-08-29 return is 48 months back; -> 268.47); claim_free_credit (P) 2% (-> 268.47); umbrella_account_credit (P, cross umbrella) 3% (-> 271.30). Whole baseline 290.17. payment: pay_in_full_discount (P, multi-source) 3% (-> 312.12); late_renewal_charge (M: per-day accrual vs flat vs none) 21 days x 1.25 = 26.25 (-> 277.99); member_dividend_lines (P, cross home/umbrella) 4% (-> 314.75); electronic_payment_credit (P, multi-source) all electronic within 36 months (2024-08-16 EFT, 2025-08-20 card) -> 1.5% (near-miss: the 2023-08-22 check is 37 months back; counting it gives the mixed tier; -> 308.18). Whole baseline 300.32 (premium + fee + earlier balance). Stamps: premium_balance -12.50 agrees with the ledger and no rule reads it.
[Overwrites] offer supersedes the base building-premium sentence, the annual-premium sentence, the indicated-premium half of the renewal-rating sentence ('At renewal the indicated premium is rated on the zone, elevation and limits on file on the renewal offer date') of flood_premium_rating and the companion sentence of flood_agg_companion_discount; renewal supersedes the other half ('the renewal term premium is the smaller of that indicated premium and the expiring term_premium increased by renewal_rate_cap_pct, rounded half-up to the cent.'); payment supersedes nothing (base fixes no payment amount). Every other base clause (policy fee never discounted, minimum premium, grace period) is inherited.
[Seed] customer; flood policy; 15 billing rows over four terms; 5 claim rows; HomeGuard (companion, era, dividend, umbrella schedule key); umbrella + 2 underlying rows (account credit, dividend). No row lights an obligation outside the tree: all terms settle, the 2024 claim is closed by denial, the 2021 claim closed.
[Persona] Retired librarian, embarrassed about the missed bill; volunteers only the goal, card, no changes; gives phone/DOB/ZIP/email/policy number/other policies only when asked; passive reactions: 'go ahead' when told something must be set up first, pays exactly the stated amount on the handed-over step, reads back the confirmation number, ends on confirmation. She never states a figure (she only remembers 'around three hundred dollars').
[Reachability] Every action runs at frozen_time 2026-09-24 10:15; nothing waits on mail, a lender, or a date. The payment confirmation number is produced by the user tool and enters the transcript.
[Standard solution] find_customers(phone) -> verify(phone, DOB) -> reads (policy, billing, claims, endorsements, HomeGuard, LandlordGuard, umbrella, underlying) -> offer 453.57 -> renewal 2026-09-03..2027-09-03 term 262.82, fee 50.00, payer insured -> hand over the payment 304.24 by card.
[Verification] Values produced by the gate's own evaluator (check_compute.build_env/eval_compute) on the handling-time world of each step: offer 453.57, renewal 262.82, payment 304.24; factor and baseline figures as above; check_compute --task 0 recomputes the same.
[Draft recomputation from visible context] From the KB prose (the three policy rules), tool schemas and the read returns only: payment waits on a new-term charge -> absent -> renewal waits on an indicated premium -> empty -> record the offer (rating rules give 453.57) -> renewal (tenure clock from the 2021 claim payment, tenured cap 12%, credits 7% give 262.82) -> payment (earlier credit, discount, dividend, electronic credit, per-day late charge give 304.24). Same as gold.
[Revision round 2 — audit audits/policy_task/flood_coverage_and_mortgagee_billing] R-0-1/F-G1: cap_claim_window (a window constant swapped in one COUNT, i.e. a parameter) removed; replaced by cap_tenure_start, a genuine anchor-family method (household HomeGuard start / most recent claim payment / original effective date); the cap ladder values became tier cap less 7 / less 3 so no tier is above the default on any tier (closes O-G8d). Term premium 253.43 -> 262.82. R-0-2/F-G2: earlier_balance_treatment (two tiers, one signed addition) removed as a factor; the earlier balance now enters through the baseline paragraph (owed added, credit deducted; a third-party credit is left for refund), and the late-renewal charge became the method factor (per-day accrual above 15 days, flat charge 1-15 days, none otherwise); a fourth factor, the electronic-payment credit, was added. Payment 298.19 -> 306.87. R-0-3: the indication factor_trace plumbing line now reads RND(493.007414 x 0.92) = 453.57. O-0-1: edge renewal <- offer re-declared state_gate with gate flood_policies.indicated_renewal_premium, closure texts corrected. O-G1: each overwrite now quotes only its half of rating S5. O-G3a/b/d/e, O-G6a applied in the charter. Kept as observations (reasons in the difficulty worklog): O-0-2/O-G7 (discount, dividend, electronic credit and late charge settle inside the payment and no event type exists to post them; after gold the account shows a small credit below no rule's action), O-0-3 (a real near-miss now exists: the 2023 EFT payment just outside the electronic window), O-G5.
[Revision round 3 — audit revision_2] N-G1: the payment <- renewal edge's condition and effect now say what the compute reads (before the renewal new_term_premium is the expiring term's own charge, 252.32 here; the renewal moves effective_date to 2026-09-03 and posts the new charge); closure condition and why_false updated to match. R2-0-1: the [Business-object card] now reads charges 1882.56 incl. the new term's 262.82 premium and 50.00 fee. O-0-3: the 2023-08-22 payment is now a check and the 2024-08-16 payment an EFT, so the in-window payments are all electronic (1.5%) and the check 37 months back is a near-miss that moves the tier (a reader who counts it lands on mixed, 0.5%); payment 306.87 -> 304.24, baseline 300.32 unchanged, factor figures 312.12 / 277.99 / 314.75 / 308.18. N-G3: the late-charge sentence now says the daily charge is multiplied by every calendar day from the new term's start date. N-G5: the electronic credit reads only the named insured's own payments (payer insured), so a lender's escrow check is outside it. O-G3b: the LandlordGuard read now filters the property address.
user_scenario: You are Rosalind Achterberg-Nwosu, a retired school librarian who has lived at 118 Riverbend Lane, Loveland, OH 45140 since 2009, calling Larkspur Mutual about the flood insurance on that house. Every July a flood renewal bill comes in the mail and you pay it; this year nothing came, and while filing papers this week you noticed the declarations page says the flood policy ran to September 3, 2026. You are a little embarrassed and a little worried, and you open by saying you want to pay the flood renewal today so the coverage carries on — you will pay it yourself, by card, on this call. You do not want anything about the coverage changed; keep it exactly as it is. You pay your own bills; no bank or lender is involved with this policy any more. You give details only as they are asked for: your phone number is 740-518-2936, your date of birth is 1968-03-17, and if asked for more, your ZIP code is 45140 and your email is rachterberg.nwosu@brushcreekmail.com. If the agent asks which policy, it is the flood policy on the Riverbend Lane house, number FG-5207-4418. If asked whether you have other Larkspur policies, you say yes, your homeowners policy on the same house and a personal umbrella, and you have no rental property. You do not remember what you paid last year beyond 'around three hundred dollars'. If the agent explains that something has to be set up or worked out on their side before you can pay, you say that is fine and ask them to go ahead, and you wait while they do it. You do not know how the premium is worked out and you never suggest a figure; if the agent mentions a late charge or a discount, you simply say 'all right' and let them carry on. Once the agent tells you the amount to pay and hands the payment over to you, you pay exactly that amount by card on the payment step they give you, and you read back the confirmation number it gives you if they ask. When the agent confirms the payment went through and your flood coverage continues, you thank them warmly and end the call; you do not ask for anything else.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.indicated_renewal_premium: 453.57. Rated amount 238000.00 (limit 250000.00 exceeds replacement cost 238000.00: rated on the replacement cost); building rate 1.45 (zone AE, map revision 2025-08-12 is 13 months before 2026-09-24, fewer than 24: newly mapped rate); building premium 238000/1000 x 1.45 x 1.04 = 358.904; loss load 5% (one claim payment 2021-04-14 inside 120 months, none inside 36); construction-era load +10% (HomeGuard HG3-5148-2291 at the same address, year built 1962 < 1975); elevation credit 5% (certificate at_or_above_1ft but a claim payment within 120 months: 10 x 0.5); adjusted building 358.904 x 1.05 x 1.10 x 0.95 = 393.807414; contents 80000/1000 x 1.24 = 99.20; companion 8% (HomeGuard at the same address in force 208 months >= 60: 5 + 3); (393.807414 + 99.20) x 0.92 = 453.5669 -> 453.57, above the 250.00 minimum. Every input is a record the reads return, so any agent applying the published rule converges on 453.57.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.flood_policy_id: Value b77deded-a4c6-4898-9b0d-d89d143716b3. Basis: same flood policy lookup return as the offer; the renewal acts on FG-5207-4418. Unique: one flood policy.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.new_expiration_date: 2027-09-03. Basis: flood_policy_renewed 'The policy renews for twelve months' and the blueprint 'Every policy is a twelve-month contract'; twelve months from 2026-09-03 is 2027-09-03. Unique: one twelve-month term.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.term_premium: 262.82. Indicated 453.57 is on file once the offer is recorded; tenure for the cap restarts at the most recent flood claim payment 2021-04-14 (a claim payment lies inside the 120-month lookback), 65 whole months to 2026-09-24; no claim payment within 60 months; so the cap is the tenured tier: 15 - 3 = 12% -> capped 252.32 x 1.12 = 282.60; smaller of 453.57 and 282.60 = 282.60; credits: prompt payment 2% (no returned payment within 36 months — the 2022-08-29 return is 48 months back — and the 2025-08-20 payment precedes the 2025-09-03 due date), claim-free 2% (a claim payment exists but none in 60 months), account 3% (umbrella PU-5073-6614 in force lists HG3-5148-2291 and never removed it) = 7%; 282.60 x 0.93 = 262.818 -> 262.82.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.policy_fee: 50.00. Basis: FloodGuard Standard tier parameter policy_fee 50.00 and flood_premium_rating 'the policy fee is charged on top of it each term and is never discounted'; the base event flood_policy_renewed triggers flood_fee_assessed with fee_code policy_fee. Unique: one tier value.

argument_uniqueness_tracing.amount: 304.24. New-term premium charge 262.82 plus policy fee 50.00 (posted by the renewal); earlier balance -12.50 (charges 1882.56 less payments and credits 1582.24 less the new term's 312.82), a credit made by the insured's own payment, deducted; pay-in-full 3% of 262.82 = 7.88 (annual plan, >= 250); member dividend 4% = 10.51 (HomeGuard and umbrella in force); electronic-payment credit 1.5% = 3.94 (the named insured's payments within 36 months are an EFT and a card payment and no check; the 2023-08-22 check is 37 months back); late-renewal charge per day 1.25 x 21 = 26.25 (21 calendar days from 2026-09-03, more than 15); 262.82 + 50.00 - 12.50 - 7.88 - 10.51 - 3.94 + 26.25 = 304.24.
argument_uniqueness_tracing.payment_method: card. Basis: the caller's line 'you will pay it yourself, by card, on this call'; the docstring 'card when the insured pays with a debit or credit card'. eft, check, mortgagee_check and none are excluded by her stated choice (and mortgagee_check/none never apply to an insured's own payment).

edges.condition: The policy's effective_date is the start of the new term (the expiring term's expiration date) and flood_billing carries a flood_premium_billed entry whose term_effective_date is that date; while the policy still shows the expiring term, the only premium charge matching its effective_date is the expiring term's own charge, which is not a charge for the new term.
edges.policy_source: A renewal payment is not taken until the premium account carries the premium charge for the new term.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The policy still shows the expiring term (effective_date 2025-09-03); the only premium charge matching it is that term's own charge, already billed and paid. No charge exists for the term starting 2026-09-03 and the policy's effective_date is not yet that date.
unresolved_at_frozen_time.flips_to_true_by: The renewal posts a flood_premium_billed charge 262.82 (with a 50.00 policy fee) for term 2026-09-03 and moves the policy's effective_date to 2026-09-03, so new_term_premium becomes 262.82.

edges.condition: flood_policies.indicated_renewal_premium carries the indicated premium for the upcoming term (it is empty on a policy whose renewal offer was never recorded).
edges.policy_source: The renewal term premium is fixed only after the indicated premium for the upcoming term stands on the policy.

unresolved_at_frozen_time.why_false: The policy carries no indicated renewal premium: the offer due 2026-07-05 was never recorded.

prerequisite_closure.order_uniqueness: A chain, no parallel prerequisites: offer -> renewal -> payment. The payment reads the new-term charge the renewal posts (value dependency); the renewal needs the indicated premium the offer records to be present at all (a state gate: on this world the capped premium 282.60 is the smaller figure, so any indicated premium of 282.60 or more gives the same term premium). No other order leaves the same terminal state: without the offer no indicated premium stands on the policy and the renewal clears nothing it recorded.

edge_load_bearing.skipped_effect: Skipping the renewal leaves no new-term charge and the old term's dates: the payment formula reads the expiring term (252.32 + 50.00) with 386 late days and gives 448.56 instead of 304.24; the policy keeps term 2025-09-03 with term_premium 252.32 (terminal hash differs).

State gate: skipping the offer leaves indicated_renewal_premium empty, so the smaller-of comparison has no indicated premium and the renewal term premium cannot be fixed (the recompute raises); the terminal policy row also differs (the offer's field write is missing). As a value it does not move the term premium on this world, because the capped 282.60 is the smaller figure.

prerequisite_closure.no_user_hint: The persona only asks to pay the flood renewal by card and keep coverage unchanged; it never mentions a renewal offer, an indicated premium, a renewal record or a new-term charge, and asks nothing like 'does something need setting up first'. It reacts only after the agent says something must be done on their side ('that is fine ... go ahead').
prerequisite_closure.tools_do_not_block: record_flood_renewal_offer_81f1ff73, renew_flood_policy_8cc307a9 and pay_flood_renewal_premium_ad8d78a5 each perform one ctx.update/ctx.create with the given values and read nothing but the policy's customer_id; the payment tool posts a payment even when no new-term charge exists and the renewal tool writes a term premium even when no indicated premium is on file — no check, no refusal, no hint.
